slug: 2021-09-13 The burden of recording and reporting health data in primary health care facilities in five low- and lower-middle income countries

facts.fact: A five-country study led with the Ministry of Health (Siyam et al., BMC Health Services Research) found in 2016-17 that Mozambique's public primary care facilities tallied paper registers onto monthly paper reporting forms (52 mandated, the most of the five countries; 25 in use) submitted to the district management office, where the forms' data were entered into the district management information system.
facts.system: routine health information system (district management information system)

facts.fact: The same study states that none of the selected facilities had electronic data collection in place in 2016-17: 0 of the 16 randomly selected public primary care facilities visited in Mozambique (15 health centres and 1 health post, in four districts), and 0 of 80 across the five countries.
facts.system: routine health information system (district management information system)

facts.fact: Siyam et al. report that in 2016-17 patient data at the 16 Mozambican public primary care facilities visited (15 health centres and 1 health post) were recorded daily in paper registers and tally sheets, recording taking 53% of consultation time, and that none of the selected facilities had an electronic system.
facts.system: patient registers at primary care facilities (paper)

systems.system: routine health information system (district management information system)
systems.tiers: health centres and health posts report on paper to the district management office, which keys the data
